title: Nicholls hundred and Phillips's 94 rescue New Zealand to 243 for five after Bumrah burst
dek: New Zealand were 70 for five in Wellington before an unbeaten 173-run stand; India, who chose to bowl, went wicketless for the last 53 overs of the first day.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips turned the first day of the first Test in Wellington on its head, adding an unbeaten 173 for the sixth wicket to take New Zealand from 70 for five to 243 for five at stumps on Thursday, after Jasprit Bumrah had torn through the top order. Nicholls was 113 not out off 221 balls, with 14 fours, and Phillips was six short of a century on 94 off 182 balls, with 13 fours.

India won the toss and chose to bowl at the Basin Reserve, and for two sessions the decision looked sound. Bumrah bowled New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck in the first over and finished the day with three for 52 from 17 overs. But India could not take a wicket in the last 53 overs of the day.

## How the day went

Devon Conway went for 4, caught behind by Rishabh Pant off Anshul Kamboj, to leave New Zealand 12 for two. Rachin Ravindra made 15 before edging Akash Deep to Pant, and Bumrah then removed Daryl Mitchell for 1, caught by Yashasvi Jaiswal at forward short leg, and Tom Blundell for 5, caught by Shubman Gill at first slip. At 70 for five early in the second session, New Zealand were in danger of being bowled out for well under 150.

Nicholls and Phillips took them to 140 for five at tea, scoring slowly but rarely looking troubled, and then batted through the whole of the final session as Gill rotated his bowlers. Nicholls reached his century late in the day. Their stand, made off 322 balls, dwarfs every other partnership of the innings; the next best was 39, for the third wicket. India's other bowlers went wicketless after the morning: Prasidh Krishna had none for 58 from 16 overs and Washington Sundar, the only specialist spinner, none for 38 from 16. Kamboj finished with one for 57 and Akash Deep with one for 33.

"It was really nice," Nicholls said of his hundred after play, according to reports, adding that Phillips's energy at the crease was "infectious".

## Selection

India went in with four fast bowlers and one spinner, as Gill had said they would on Tuesday. Mohammed Siraj, the uncapped Gurnoor Brar and Ravindra Jadeja were left out, reports said; Kamboj and Krishna were preferred to Siraj. Pant, back from injury, kept wicket. New Zealand are without their white-ball captain Mitchell Santner, who fractured his hand in the final one-day international.

## What is at stake

The two-Test series counts towards the 2025-27 World Test Championship, in which New Zealand lead the table and India are fourth. Gill has said India need to win five or six of their remaining seven Tests to reach the final. The second Test is in Christchurch.

## What happens next

Day two begins at 3.30 am IST on Friday. New Zealand's last four batters, Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry and Jacob Duffy, are still to come, and India have the second new ball available from the start of Friday's play, with Phillips six runs short of his hundred.
